title: Chapter 12: Local Self Government – Panchayati Raj and Municipalities

blocks.content: The Gram Sabha is a body consisting of persons registered in the electoral rolls relating to a village comprised within the area of Panchayat at the village level.

rows: Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti, Zila Parishad
Nagar Panchayat, Municipal Council, Municipal Corporation

items: Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) recommended the establishment of a three-tier Panchayati Raj system and is known as the architect of Panchayati Raj in India.
Rajasthan was the first state to establish Panchayati Raj, inaugurated in Nagaur district on October 2, 1959, followed by Andhra Pradesh.
State Finance Commission is constituted every 5 years under Article 243-I to review the financial position of local bodies.
The minimum age required to contest local body elections (Panchayat/Municipality) is 21 years, unlike Legislative Assemblies which require 25 years.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts of 1992 granted constitutional status to rural and urban local self-governments respectively.
Part IX (Articles 243 to 243O) and the 11th Schedule cover Panchayati Raj Institutions with 29 functional matters.
Part IXA (Articles 243P to 243ZG) and the 12th Schedule cover Urban Local Bodies with 18 functional matters.
A 3-tier Panchayati Raj system exists at the Village, Intermediate (Block), and District levels for states with a population exceeding 20 lakhs.
Elections to local bodies are conducted every 5 years by the independent State Election Commission.
